messages:
alex: thinking out loud — should the console surface SLO alert rules as editable objects or keep them as read-only generated from policy? we keep getting tickets about noisy pages when teams set low thresholds.
tara: +1 to editable, but only if we add sane defaults and a scope selector. teams shouldn't be able to accidentally page p0 for tiny blips.
sam: can we expose both? editable per-team overrides, with a tenant-wide guardrail. UI could show "effective" rule and the source (global vs override).
priya: the real pain is notification routing. right now an SLO breach pings the default oncall — we need routing by route/tenant and a soft fanout to Slack threads first, only page if the error_budget burn rate is sustained.
jesse: agree. proposal: two-stage notify: first -> console/channel (non-pager) + ops-snooze window; second -> page if window > X and burn rate > Y. Also add suppression for deployments.
alex: sketch of YAML people liked in backend meeting:

```yaml
rule_name: api_error_budget_low
scope: tenant:my-product, route:/v1/generate
window: 5m
threshold: 2.0 # percent errors
burn_rate: 3.0
notify_first: ["#redwood-slo-alerts", "email:eng-team@redwood.com"]
notify_page_if: { sustained_minutes: 10, burn_rate: 4.0 }
suppress_on_event: ["deploy", "planned_maintenance"]
```

tara: where do we get the events for suppress_on_event? deploy pipeline posts to events bus but we need the console to subscribe; otherwise suppressions will miss quick rollouts.

ops-bot: FYI: events bus has a `deployment.*` topic. we can add a subscription filter for `deployment.*` + tenant tag.

priya: also important — quota-driven SLOs. if a tenant hits quota and we throttle, that looks like an error. we should surface cause: throttled vs 5xx.

sam: telemetry change: add `slo_reason` tag to emitted traces/metrics (throttle|backend_error|timeout|client_error) so console can group alerts and avoid noisy duplicates.

jesse: small internal-api debate: should the alerting backend expose a REST `/slo-rules` or a controller-based RPC? Teams will want to patch overrides programmatically.

alex: prefer REST for self-serve but hide write endpoints behind a feature-flag + entitlement check. Also need audit logs (who changed what, when).

priya: UX ask: in the console show a small simulation panel — "If this rule existed historically, would it have paged?" lets teams preview noise impact before enabling.

tara: love the sim idea. also add a suggested threshold slider with historical percentile guidance (p95 latency, p99 error spikes).

deploy-bot: deploy finished: infra/slo-alerts v2.1 -> prod at 2026-03-18T14:02:10Z :rocket:

alex: next steps: jesse + sam to draft REST contract + telemetry tags, priya + tara to prototype sim UI, ops to hook events bus into suppressions. I'll open a tiny RFC and link here.

ops-bot: RFC draft: https://go/redwood/rfc/slo-alerts-console-suppressions (editable)

sam: I'll take the API stub this week. tagging @jesse for routing logic.

jesse: got it. will add routing matrix and default fanout behavior. will also add a safe-mode toggle that converts pages -> slack DMs until teams opt-in.

alex: perfect. thanks all :thumbsup:
